static_traits.name: Chen Ran
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships affected, hard to form meaningful connections; uncomfortable seeking help from friends and acquaintances, weak social support
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; has not yet received treatment or counseling for similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Highly cooperative, clear expression, capable of self-reflection; low mood with a sense of hopelessness when presenting complaints, willing to try new approaches

basic_info.main_problem: I have a hard time getting along with my family and always feel I will live alone forever.
basic_info.core_demands: These unresolved family problems and feelings of loneliness are affecting my mental health and overall well-being, which prompts me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Over the past years, family gatherings or daily discussions often escalated into arguments; the client describes herself as 'walking on thin ice' in the family, having tried calm communication and compromise to ease conflicts, but without lasting effect; prolonged conflict has made her feel increasingly lonely and hopeless, with pessimistic anticipation about future interpersonal relationships.

core_beliefs: I am flawed / I have fundamental problems
I am not needed / not worthy of being loved
I am destined to be isolated

special_situations.event: During family gatherings or family discussions, topics easily escalate into arguments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If we cannot reach agreement, it means the relationship has failed, and it also shows something is wrong with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Restrains oneself in advance, communicates as calmly as possible, and proactively compromises to avoid conflict escalation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, it is useless; things always get out of control

special_situations.event: Thinking about future living and life situations when being alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even get along with family, I will be unable to build good relationships with anyone
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowers expectations of the relationship, 'preserving' a minimum of harmony through more self-compromise

special_situations.event: Casual comments from family or differing opinions arise
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they object or criticize, it means they hate me / I am not accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Rushing to explain, apologize, or give in, to reduce the risk of being negated

special_situations.event: Recalling occasional pleasant moments in family interactions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative experiences are more numerous and more real; the few positive moments are not representative
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or downplays positive evidence and focuses on the negative to avoid 'self-deception'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good moments are rare and will not change anything

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood, accepted, and close to family, to have a stable and warm connection
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and blamed, fearing the relationship spiraling out of control and being isolated, ending up alone forever
defense_goal: Avoiding conflict and being rejected through restraint and compromise
Turning dissatisfaction and aggression against the self to maintain surface stability in the relationship

object_relations.self_representation: A flawed, easily disliked isolate / blamed one
object_relations.object_representation: Family members experienced as picky, hostile, hard to communicate with, and not understanding her

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to examine evidence, focus on positive moments in the family, or offers different perspectives
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting exploration as minimizing or negating her pain, then turning to self-blame ('it is all my fault') to keep the relationship safe
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaking in a self-blaming tone, lowering her voice, using expressions like 'it is all my fault / I did wrong', reducing emotional expression, avoiding dissatisfaction with others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the specific details of family conflict and the current emotional experience
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Replacing specific emotional and need expressions with generalized, abstract narratives, keeping rational distance to reduce anxiety
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using abstract, generalized language (e.g. 'things escalated'), avoiding touching on specific feelings and details, in a steady tone with few emotional words.

manifestations: Isolation and alienation caused by long-term conflict with family
Hard to build meaningful connections with others, weak social support
outcomes: Sense of hopelessness and negative anticipation of the future
Low mood and intensified sense of isolation
Treads on thin ice in interpersonal interaction; avoids touching real needs

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: 'Walking on thin ice' in the family, overly cautious to avoid conflict
Tending toward self-blame ('I must have done something wrong'), repressing her own needs to maintain surface harmony

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Easily interprets interactions as 'they must hate me'
Attributing the internal experience of self-denial to others' negative intentions

exception_events.target_problem: During family gatherings or discussions, the client usually argues with family and feels isolated, afterwards experiencing hopelessness and frustration.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In individual family interactions, there were pleasant exchanges or shared laughter, with a relatively relaxed atmosphere; unlike usual, it did not quickly escalate into arguments, and the client's sense of isolation lessened in the moment.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the topics were lighter, members' emotions calmer; the interaction pace slower with fewer interruptions; the client tried expressing herself calmly and listening to others, thus reducing tension.

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to seek help and try new methods (such as accepting behavioral experiments)
Has self-reflection capacity, able to identify negative automatic thoughts and thinking patterns
Has had a few positive interaction experiences as objective evidence for change
Willing to communicate and compromise, with some willingness and skill to maintain relationships
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases: catastrophizing and predicting the future, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking
Stable self-denial belief ('I am flawed / not loved')
Weak social support system, unwilling to seek help from friends or acquaintances
Hopelessness and negative attentional bias from a long history of family conflict
Continuously maintains excessive vigilance and self-restraint in interpersonal interactions (as if walking on thin ice)

target_behavior.behavior: In family interactions, treads on thin ice, excessively avoids sensitive topics and self-expression
antecedent: Casual comments from family or differing opinions arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Threat appraisal driven by fear of being rejected and losing control of the relationship, and the core belief of 'I am flawed / not loved'
target_behavior.function: Escapes conflict and negative evaluation, briefly maintaining subjective safety and superficial relationship stability
target_behavior.consequence: Genuine communication restricted, relationships grow more distant, loneliness and hopelessness intensify

target_behavior.behavior: Negative predictions and mind-reading-style self-talk (such as 'I will live alone forever' or 'they must hate me')
antecedent: Thinking about future living and life situations when being alone
Ruminating on interaction details after family conflicts
target_behavior.core_reason: Low sense of external control over the future; threat anticipation maintained by overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking
target_behavior.function: Gaining cognitive 'certainty' and mentally preparing for the worst (superficially reducing uncertainty anxiety)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and hopelessness rise, reducing motivation to try improving relationships further
